name: Damona

attributes.attribute: consort of Borvo and Apollo Moritasgus
name likely means great or divine ox
honoured at the healing springs and warm baths of Alesia
signed by the snake and grain she shared with Hygeia and Demeter
stands beside Apollo Borvon, Apollo Moritasgus, and Albius
worshipped with Borvo at the shrine of Bourbonne-les-Bains in north-eastern France
the consort of Borvo when he is known as Bormanus
several commentators see the cult of the cow in her worship

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Damona is a Gaulish goddess whose name likely means great or divine ox. People honoured her alone and beside several male gods, including Apollo Borvon, Apollo Moritasgas, and the god Albius. A walled precinct at Alesia held sacred springs and warm baths. Finds there included a stone head of her crowned with ears of grain. A hand gripping a snake came from the same precinct. Bound to healing waters, she carried the snake and grain signs she shared with Hygeia and Demeter.

okr.objective: Document Damona, the Gaulish healing goddess of the springs at Alesia.
key_results: Record Damona as a Gaulish goddess whose name may mean great or divine ox.
Note her company beside Apollo Borvon, Apollo Moritasgus, and Albius.
